title: arXiv AI papers — Friday, 9 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred editorial selection based on paper relevance and reported evaluation, not measured popularity. Semantic Scholar showed zero citations and zero influential citations for all eight papers at the 2026-10-12 00:10 UTC snapshot.

sections.title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
sections.abstract: The authors train activation probes on a large falsehood dataset and report strong detection results for agentic sabotage and hidden-goal deception, including up to 98.8% AUC on SHADE-Arena and up to 99.7% in one introspective evaluation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper claims that probes aggregating signals across model layers and tokens can scale to frontier-monitoring settings and detect some deception not evident from the transcript alone.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say FIBS contains little reasoning (5.5% of rows), is mostly off-policy, and is largely artificial; the reported results do not establish reliable deployment performance on naturally occurring deception.

sections.title: OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport
sections.abstract: OnTrack compares an agent’s evolving, dependency-aware execution graph with successful reference runs, aiming to flag or stop failures online; on SWE-bench trajectories, the authors report improved early ranking of failing runs and compute savings from an abort policy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a streaming optimal-transport monitor that can operate with different levels of prior information, from successful reference traces down to event logs alone.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline outcome results are on SWE-bench trajectories; performance in other agent domains and live deployments is not established by that evaluation.

sections.title: Searching for “Harmful Refusal”: A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
sections.abstract: The authors test whether HELM Safety’s harmful-refusal scores measure one coherent attribute; their analyses find saturation in three candidate datasets and evidence that HarmBench scores do not isolate a single attribute.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper argues that a safety score should demonstrate construct validity before being interpreted as a measurement of one attribute or used to compare models.
sections.unique_caveat: The audit focuses on four HELM Safety datasets and the HarmBench analysis; its findings do not by themselves establish how every safety benchmark behaves.

sections.title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons—a statistical look at the METR plot
sections.abstract: Using 228 software tasks and 26 AI systems, the authors refit METR time horizons with spline and item-response models, finding a nonlinear mapping between human task time and estimated AI difficulty and proposing diagnostic plots for interpreting the metric.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide alternative time-horizon estimates and construct-validity diagnostics, and caution that equal multiplicative jumps in “human time” need not represent equal difficulty changes.
sections.unique_caveat: The analysis is anchored to METR’s software-engineering task set; the authors specifically recommend interpreting time horizons together with diagnostics, especially when extending the benchmark.

sections.title: DreamTrue: Action-Faithful Robot World Model with Counterfactual Post-Training
sections.abstract: DreamTrue combines geometric action conditioning, counterfactual trajectory post-training, and a learned video reward model to improve robot-world-model predictions; the authors report first place in the AgiBot World Challenge 2026 world-model track and a lower human-assessed interaction-defect rate.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim counterfactual post-training broadens the model’s action/contact coverage and improves physical plausibility without paired ground-truth futures.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract’s quantitative evaluation and challenge result are tied to AgiBot; transfer to other robot platforms and broader task distributions remains to be demonstrated.

sections.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
sections.abstract: BrickBench evaluates text-conditioned agents that must design LEGO assemblies satisfying semantic, design, and physical-build constraints, with scores for validity, alignment, and design across three settings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce BrickBench and BrickAgent, and report that current leading agents meet many verifiable requirements but remain below human designs.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation is specific to LEGO-part selection and assembly; success on this benchmark alone would not establish general physical-design competence.

sections.title: Dex-One2Many: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Human Demonstration
sections.abstract: Dex-One2Many turns one human video into scene-graph constraints for reinforcement learning, then transfers a simulation-trained dexterous manipulation policy zero-shot to a real multi-fingered hand; the authors evaluate five tasks and report a larger advantage in unseen configurations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim scene-graph constraints improve guided RL exploration while supporting generalization to unseen poses and grasps from a single human video.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported results cover five tasks and one real multi-fingered-hand transfer setting; broader hardware and task coverage is still needed.

sections.title: VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression
sections.abstract: VFold merges similar value-cache states across transformer layers using symmetry-aware reparameterization, with the stated aim of reducing long-context KV-cache memory without architectural changes or major decoding overhead.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose cross-layer value-cache merging and claim it can combine with existing compression methods to reach higher compression ratios at minimal additional cost.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not give a concrete compression ratio or workload-level savings figure, so the practical magnitude cannot be judged from the abstract alone.
